note.title: Northanger Abbey — plot, characters and Gothic subversion
note.overview: Understand the novel’s plot and use Gothic convention/subversion to build thematic interpretations.
learningGoals: Know the main plot arc and relationships.
Explain how Catherine’s imagination shapes her judgement.
mustMemoriseRules: Austen can use a convention and question it at the same time.
Catherine’s mistaken interpretation is evidence about reading, imagination and judgement.
Plot incidents should be connected to a thematic claim.
workedExamples: A threatening setting can invite a Gothic reading before an ordinary explanation undercuts it.
Catherine’s growth involves learning to distinguish imaginative possibility from supported judgement.
commonMistakes: Retelling Catherine’s mistake without analysing its purpose.
Assuming comedy means the episode has no serious thematic function.
detailedExplanation: The curriculum scope is verified against the official Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 English Curriculum Outline 2026-27.
Northanger Abbey is in the public domain; this bank mainly uses paraphrase and app-written scenarios so practice focuses on reasoning rather than memorising quotations.
Long whole-text essay tasks are practice/self-check and do not by themselves create formal Mastery evidence.
examTips: Keep Gothic convention and Austen’s subversion in the same sentence where possible.
Use plot detail as evidence for an argument, not as a substitute for one.
Comment on form and structure as well as language where relevant.
Context should explain a tension or convention, not sit separately.
quickCheck: Know the main plot arc and relationships.
Explain how Catherine’s imagination shapes her judgement.
beforeStartingPractice: Recall the main plot arc and Gothic expectations before practising.
